key_insight: A physics-informed Fourier-wavelet transformer improves multiscale CFD surrogate modeling by combining spectral encoding, PDE-residual-guided attention, and self-supervised physics pretraining to better reconstruct localized flow structures.
engineering_relevance: The model offers a practical way to accelerate real-world fluid simulations while preserving near-body, wake-core, and far-wake dynamics needed for engineering analysis and design.
method: Hybrid Fourier-wavelet spectral encoding for multiscale flow representation
Physics-biased self-attention driven by PDE residual diagnostics
Self-supervised pretraining with Masked Physics Prediction and Equation Consistency Prediction
evidence_signal: Evaluated on two real benchmarks—cylinder wake and fluid-structure interaction—the model achieved best aggregate accuracy, including 0.05875 NMSE and 0.97019 PCC on cylinder wake, and 2.70×10^-4 NMSE on FSI versus 4.02×10^-4 for the strongest baseline.
watch_item: Performance is reported for next-step velocity-field reconstruction under a shared local protocol, so generalization to longer rollouts or different flow regimes may require additional validation.
paper_title: A Physics-Informed Fourier-Wavelet Transformer for Multiscale Computational Fluid Dynamics Surrogate Modeling
